sources.entry: ArchiveBox - Create HTML & screenshot archives of sites from your bookmarks, browsing history, RSS feeds, or other sources (alternative to Wayback Machine). (Source Code) MIT Python/Docker
ArchiveBox | Self-hosted internet archiving of websites, media and more

summary.one_liner: ArchiveBox is a self-hosted web archiving app that saves snapshots of URLs from bookmarks, browser history, RSS feeds, and other sources in standard formats like HTML, PDF, PNG, and WARC.
summary.what_it_does: ArchiveBox takes URLs one at a time or from scheduled imports (bookmarks, history, RSS, Pocket/Pinboard, browser extension, and more) and saves multiple snapshot formats per page, including original HTML, SingleFile HTML, screenshot PNG, PDF, WARC, title, favicon, and article text. It detects embedded content and extracts it, such as YouTube/SoundCloud media via yt-dlp, git clones of GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket repos, and social media post text and comments. Data is stored as ordinary files plus a SQLite index in a single collection folder. It can be used through a Docker-based web UI, a CLI, a Python API, a REST API (alpha), or direct filesystem and SQL access. It also supports optional archive.org submission for redundancy, and can be set to local-only mode. Access control options include public or private permissions, and support for archiving pages that need login or cookies.
use_cases: saving web pages before they disappear
backing up videos and audio from YouTube or SoundCloud
saving research papers and documents from the web
keeping a private alternative to the Wayback Machine
how_to_run: docker compose exec archivebox archivebox add '<url>'
pip/uv: uv tool install --python 3.13 --prerelease explicit --upgrade 'archivebox>=0.9.0rc0' then archivebox init && archivebox install
notable: Saves many redundant formats per page (HTML, PDF, PNG, WARC, SingleFile, JSON) in standard, human-readable files
Scheduled and recursive imports from RSS, bookmarks, and browser history with an orchestrator built into archivebox server
Browser extension, macOS/iOS apps, and a chat bot as input routes
Data stored as plain files and a SQLite index, readable without ArchiveBox running
Docker Compose, uv, brew, apt, and several community distributions available
caveats: Disk use ranges from about 1 GB to 50 GB per 1000 snapshots, mostly driven by audio/video saving
Windows is not officially supported without Docker or WSL; community distributions may lag the official channels
Archived pages may contain private cookies or tokens and archived JavaScript is untrusted, so access controls must be configured carefully
